22: ## 1. WHEN TO USE
23: 
24: ### Activation Triggers
25: 
26: - **Cross-AI Validation** — code review second perspective, security audit alternative analysis, bug detection, independent implementation attempts.
27: - **Cloud Handoff** — long-running tasks, complex refactors, CI-like validation, browser-dependent workflows offloaded to a cloud Devin session via `/handoff`.
28: - **Subagent Delegation** — specialized profile matches (`subagent_explore`, `subagent_general`, custom `.devin/agents/[name]/AGENT.md` profiles), parallel task processing through Devin's native subagent system.
29: - **Multi-Model Dispatch** — tasks that specifically want a model available through Devin's multi-model surface (DeepSeek, GLM-5.2, GPT-5.6 Luna Max, Grok (4.5 and 4.6), SWE-2), selected per-dispatch with `--model`.
30: - **Parallel Code Generation** — offloading generation, simultaneous code generations, background docs/test generation through subagents.
31: - **Specialized Generation** — explicit Devin requests, test suite generation, code translation, batch documentation, visual input via clipboard paste or `@` file mentions.
32: 
33: ### When NOT to Use
34: 
35: - **You ARE Devin already.** If your runtime is Devin (detection signal: `$DEVIN_PROJECT_DIR` env var set, `devin` in process ancestry, or credentials present at `~/.local/share/devin/credentials.toml` while a session is active), this skill refuses to load. Self-invocation creates a circular dispatch loop and burns tokens for no value.
36: - Simple, quick tasks where CLI overhead is not worth it, or tasks needing an immediate response (auth/network round-trips may delay).
37: - Context already loaded and understood by the current agent.
38: - Interactive refinement requiring the full-screen REPL (use `devin` directly instead).
39: - Tasks where Devin CLI is not installed.
40: 
41: ---
42: 
43: ## 2. SMART ROUTING
44: 
45: The hub's `cli-devin` mode signal routes a Devin CLI dispatch here when a request names `devin`, Cognition, an autonomous SWE dispatch, a cloud handoff or a subagent.
46: 
47: `references/cli-reference.md` and `assets/prompt-quality-card.md` load on every invocation; the hub `ROUTER.md` names the mode's first leaves.
48: 
49: Read [`ROUTER.md`](./ROUTER.md) before selecting skill-local resources; open only the matched files.
50: 
51: ---
52: 
53: ## 3. HOW IT WORKS
54: 
55: ### Prerequisites
56: 
57: Install via `devin setup` (interactive wizard) or `curl -fsSL https://devin.ai/install | bash`.
58: 
59: cli-devin authenticates through **Devin account OAuth**. Run `devin auth login` and complete the browser flow (or `--force-manual-token-flow` for SSH/remote sessions).
60: 
61: Full install, auth, flag, permission-mode, session, and troubleshooting tables live in the ALWAYS-loaded [cli-reference.md](./references/cli-reference.md). This section keeps only the routing decisions and dispatch-critical gotchas.
62: 
63: ### Execution Ownership
64: 
65: This packet owns user-facing routing, the `command -v devin` availability probe, prompt construction, and the self-invocation guard.
66: 
67: Research and review lineages delegate process construction and execution to the deep-loop runtime at `../../system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs`, using executor kind `cli-devin`. That runner accepts only the `research` and `review` loop types, so a single build or doc dispatch uses the child dispatch envelope in [providers-and-models.md](./references/providers-and-models.md) §5.
68: 
69: The runtime is the single Devin execution adapter. Do not add a packet-local wrapper, command builder, or spawn path. Direct `devin -p` snippets below are operator reference and manual-testing examples; research and review lineages use the shared runtime, and a one-shot dispatch uses the child envelope.
70: 
71: ### Provider Auth Pre-Flight (Devin Account OAuth)
72: 
73: **MANDATORY before any first dispatch in a session.** cli-devin authenticates through Devin account OAuth only. If `devin auth login` has not been completed on this machine, a dispatch fails with an authentication error mid-round-trip. Run this check once per session, cache the result, and re-run it only if a dispatch fails with an auth error.
74: 
75: ```bash
76: # One-shot pre-flight: capture Devin auth status for routing
77: DEVIN_AUTH=$(devin auth status 2>&1)
78: echo "$DEVIN_AUTH" | grep -qi "logged in" && DEVIN_AUTH_OK=1 || DEVIN_AUTH_OK=0
79: ```
80: 
81: **Decision tree** (apply in order — first match wins):
82: 
83: | State | DEVIN_AUTH_OK | Action |
84: |-------|---------------|--------|
85: | OAuth ready | 1 | Proceed with `devin -p --model <model> --permission-mode <mode> -- "<prompt>"` |
86: | Not logged in | 0 | **ASK user** to run `devin auth login` — surface the command, do NOT dispatch. Never substitute a different auth method or skip the check. |
87: 
88: **User prompt template — not logged in:**
89: 
90: ```
91: Devin is not authenticated on this machine. cli-devin uses Devin account OAuth only.
92: Run `devin auth login` (browser flow; or `devin auth login --force-manual-token-flow` for SSH/remote),
93: then confirm when login finishes — the skill will retry the original dispatch.
94: ```
95: 
96: **Error-recovery contract.** If a dispatch returns an auth error after pre-flight passed (OAuth expired or revoked), invalidate the cache, rerun `devin auth login`, and re-check before retrying. Never substitute a model the user didn't approve.
97: 
98: ### Default Invocation (Skill Default)
99: 
100: **Default model + permission mode**: `swe` (alias → `swe-2`) · `dangerous` permission mode.
101: 
102: ```bash
103: devin -p \
104:   --model swe \
105:   --permission-mode dangerous \
106:   -- \
107:   "<prompt>"
108: ```
109: 
110: > **Why `dangerous` is the default for implementation work.** Under `accept-edits` Devin may
111: > edit files but every other tool call is refused with
112: > `warning: rejected a tool call that requires confirmation`. In a non-interactive `-p` session
113: > there is nobody to confirm, so the dispatch cannot read a module to check an export, cannot
114: > grep, and cannot run the tests it was asked to run. The observed failure is not an error —
115: > it is a dispatch that spends its whole budget exploring, writes nothing, and exits 0. A
116: > caller who does not diff the worktree afterwards will read that as success.
117: >
118: > The marginal risk is smaller than the name suggests: `accept-edits` already grants arbitrary
119: > file modification, which is the destructive capability. `dangerous` adds the ability to run
120: > commands, which is what lets the executor verify its own work instead of handing back
121: > unverified edits. Use `auto` for read-only review, analysis, and research, where no
122: > elevation is needed.
123: >
124: > **`auto` is read-only, not tool-free.** It refuses any tool call that wants confirmation,
125: > and a shell command counts even when the command only reads. Observed on 2026-09-15: a
126: > crawl dispatched under `auto` decided on its own to run a `git` command to check state,
127: > was refused with `warning: rejected a tool call that requires confirmation`, and exited 0
128: > having reported almost nothing. A research dispatch that might shell out therefore needs
129: > `dangerous` with a read-only instruction in the prompt, and the caller diffs the worktree
130: > afterwards to confirm it wrote nothing. Reserve `auto` for a dispatch whose whole job is
131: > reading files.
132: 
133: **User override** (honor explicit user phrasing verbatim):
134: 
135: | User says | Resolve to |
136: |-----------|------------|
137: | (nothing specified) | `--model swe-2-max --permission-mode dangerous` |
138: | "Use glm" / "Use glm high" | `--model glm-5-2 --permission-mode dangerous` |
139: | "Use glm no-thinking" | `--model glm-5-2-none --permission-mode dangerous` |
140: | "Use glm max" | `--model glm-5-2-max --permission-mode dangerous` |
141: | "Use deepseek" | `--model deepseek-v4-flash-max --permission-mode dangerous` |
142: | "Use swe max" | `--model swe-2-max --permission-mode dangerous` |
143: | "Use glm accept-edits" | `--model glm-5-2 --permission-mode accept-edits` |
144: | "Use autonomous sandbox" | `--sandbox --permission-mode autonomous` |
145: 
146: > **Fan-out fallback:** a deep-loop lineage that pins no model runs **SWE 2 Max**. The family is named here on purpose, without a version or an effort tier, so this line does not go stale when the family ships a point release; the runner resolves the current id. A drift test keeps the two in the same family.
147: 
148: Honor the dimensions the user names. Otherwise the model stays `swe` and the permission mode stays `dangerous`.
149: 
150: ### Model Selection
151: 
152: Default `swe` (alias → `swe-2`). Switch per-dispatch with `--model <name>`; there is no headless reasoning-effort flag, so autonomy is set through `--permission-mode`.
153: 
154: Curated families, alphabetical:
155: 
156: - **DeepSeek**: `deepseek-v4-1-flash-high`, `deepseek-v4-1-flash-max`, `deepseek-v4-flash-max`.
157: - **Gemini**: `gemini-3-8-flash-high`. The uid spells the family with dashes while the Cursor scope spells the same model with dots.
158: - **GLM-5.2**: `glm-5-2` = **GLM-5.2 High**, free tier; `glm-5-2-1m` = High 1M; `glm-5-2-max` = Max; `glm-5-2-max-1m` = Max 1M; `glm-5-2-none` = No Thinking; `glm-5-2-none-1m` = No Thinking 1M.
159: - **GLM-5.3**: `glm-5-3-flash-high`, `glm-5-3-flash-max`.
160: - **GPT-5.6 Luna Max**: `gpt-5-6-luna-max`, `gpt-5-6-luna-max-priority`.
161: - **GPT-6 Luna Max**: `gpt-6-luna-max`, `gpt-6-luna-max-priority`. A separate family from GPT-5.6.
162: - **SWE-2**: `swe-2-max`, `swe-2-high`, `swe-2-medium`; free, 262K context.
163: - **SWE-1.7**: `swe-1-7`, `swe-1-7-lightning`, `swe-1-7-medium`.
164: 
165: Full roster and the permission-mode effort lever in [references/providers-and-models.md](references/providers-and-models.md).
166: 
167: **Selection Strategy**: default `swe` for quick edits and cost-sensitive work; switch to `gpt-5-6-luna-max` for reasoning-heavy work (architecture, security, deep planning); use `glm-5-2` / `glm-5-2-max` for general generation; use `swe-2-max` for max-effort SWE work. Per-task rationale table: [cli-reference.md](./references/cli-reference.md) §5.
168: 
169: ### Devin Subagent Delegation
170: 
171: The calling AI is the conductor. Devin's `run_subagent` tool spawns independent workers that share tools and codebase context but operate in their own conversation chain.
172: 
173: Two built-in profiles (`subagent_explore` read-only, `subagent_general` full-access) plus custom `.devin/agents/[name]/AGENT.md` profiles shape HOW Devin processes the subtask.
174: 
175: Full roster and invocation patterns: [agent-delegation.md](./references/agent-delegation.md).
176: 
177: | Task Type | Profile | Model |
178: |-----------|---------|-------|
179: | Read-only codebase exploration | `subagent_explore` | Default subagent model (SWE-1.6) |
180: | General-purpose code changes | `subagent_general` | Same as parent agent |
181: | Custom specialized worker | `.devin/agents/[name]/AGENT.md` | Pinned in AGENT.md or default |
182: 
183: Subagents run foreground (parent pauses) or background (parallel, auto-deny unapproved tools). The `run_subagent` tool takes a profile, not a model — to pin a model on a write-capable subagent, use a custom AGENT.md with a `model:` field.
184: 
185: ### Devin Skills, Rules, and Native Agent Profiles
186: 
187: Devin discovers the skills and rules already in the repository, and this packet adds no adapter for either.
188: 
189: A session loads the checkout's root `AGENTS.md`, cut at Devin's fixed 16,384-byte limit per rule file, because `.devin/config.json` turns the Claude import off.
190: 
191: The live `devin skills list` and `devin rules list` output is recorded in [agent-delegation.md](./references/agent-delegation.md) §10.
192: 
193: #### Agent Roster Parity
194: 
195: All 11 repo agents are dispatchable through `run_subagent`: `ai-council`, `code`, `context`, `debug`, `deep-research`, `deep-review`, `design`, `markdown`, `orchestrate`, `prompt-improver`, `review`. A live roster probe lists them alongside Devin's own `subagent_explore` and `subagent_general`.
196: 
197: Each `.devin/agents/<name>/AGENT.md` is a **symlink** to the canonical `.claude/agents/<name>.md`, matching the discovery-mirror precedent already used for `.claude/hooks/` and `.codex/hooks/`. One source of truth, so a mirror can never drift from the agent it mirrors.
198: 
199: This works because Devin's failure with Claude-format agents is a *discovery-path* limitation, not a *format-parsing* one: the same file Devin ignores at `.claude/agents/<name>.md` registers correctly once reachable at Devin's own `.devin/agents/<name>/AGENT.md` path -- Claude's `tools:` frontmatter field is accepted as-is, so no per-agent translation to `allowed-tools:` is needed.
200: 
201: Invoke by naming the profile explicitly:
202: 
203: ```bash
204: command -v devin
205: devin --permission-mode bypass -p \
206:   "Use the review subagent to review the current diff for correctness, security, and repository-convention consistency. Cite file paths and line numbers." \
207:   2>&1
208: ```
209: 
210: The experimental native profile format ([docs.devin.ai/cli/subagents](https://docs.devin.ai/cli/subagents)) and its YAML fields are in [agent-delegation.md](./references/agent-delegation.md) §5.
211: 
212: #### Installed-Version Findings
213: 
214: Devin `3000.2.17` does not import `.claude/agents/*.md` as its docs claim, so the `.devin/agents/<name>/AGENT.md` symlinks above exist, and it has no command-file system. The probes behind both findings are in [agent-delegation.md](./references/agent-delegation.md) §10.
215: 
216: ### Cloud Handoff
217: 
218: Devin's unique `/handoff` command transfers the current session to a cloud Devin session with its own VM, shell, browser, and full repo access. Use for long-running tasks, complex refactors, CI-like validation, browser-dependent workflows, and parallel execution. Full mechanics and state transfer: [cloud-handoff.md](./references/cloud-handoff.md).
219: 
220: ### Dispatch-Critical Gotchas
221: 
222: The full flag glossary, permission modes, unique capabilities (`/handoff`, `run_subagent`, `devin mcp`, session resume/continue, `--sandbox`), essential command examples, and troubleshooting table are in the ALWAYS-loaded [cli-reference.md](./references/cli-reference.md). Four gotchas that silently break a dispatch and must be honored at routing time:
223: 
224: - **`devin -p` is non-interactive and exits after one turn** — it prints the response to stdout and exits. For multi-turn work, use `devin -c` (continue) or `devin -r <session-id>` (resume). Do not expect a REPL from `-p`.
225: - **`--permission-mode` defaults to `auto` (read-only auto-approve).** File-modification tasks silently prompt or no-op without elevated mode.
226:   - Pass `--permission-mode dangerous` whenever the task requires edits.
227:   - `accept-edits` is only half a grant. It permits writes but refuses the reads and commands an implementer needs, so a dispatch under it can burn its whole budget and exit 0 having written nothing.
228:   - The `--sandbox` flag selects `autonomous` mode, the only mode available in sandbox sessions.
229: - **`devin -p` rejects MCP tool calls under `auto`/`accept-edits`** (and `smart` may be unavailable). When a least-privilege MCP allowlist is preferable to blanket elevation, grant it in a machine-local config:
230: ```json
231: // .devin/config.local.json
232: { "permissions": { "allow": ["mcp__<server>__*"] } }
233: ```
234: Then `auto`/`accept-edits` auto-approve exactly those MCP tools; reserve `dangerous` for throwaway isolated runners.
235: - **Always pass `--model` explicitly in scripts** — omitting it relies on the caller's `~/.config/devin/config.json` default, which may be a different model. Explicit means reproducible regardless of who runs it.
236: - **Model ids carry no `-high` suffix, but the interactive picker shows one** — the TUI labels `glm-5-2` as "GLM-5.2 High", so an operator asking for "GLM 5.2 high" means the id `glm-5-2`. No `glm-5-2-high` exists. `devin models list` is the authority for every id and its display name; this document's roster is a convenience copy.
237: - **A free-tier model still dispatches when the Pro quota reads 0%** — `glm-5-2` is billed as Free, and a dispatch succeeded with `Pro · 0% remaining` showing in the TUI. Quota exhaustion gates the paid families, so do not abandon a dispatch on the quota banner alone; probe with a trivial read-only call first.
238: - **`devin --help` is NOT the authoritative `--permission-mode` enum.** It prints 4 values; the binary accepts 8.
239:   - Canonical set with aliases: `normal` (`auto`), `accept-edits`, `smart`, `dangerous` (`yolo`, `bypass`), `autonomous` (requires `--sandbox`).
240:   - Do not "correct" a mode value in this skill because help omits it. That conclusion is wrong and has been reached before.
241:   - Probe instead: `devin --permission-mode <value> --prompt-file /nonexistent` (exit 2 = rejected, exit 1 = accepted).
242:   - The enum also moves between releases, so re-probe after an upgrade rather than trusting either help or this line.
243: - **Use `--` before every print-mode prompt** — `devin -p -- "list all TODO comments"` prevents the prompt from being parsed as CLI flags. The prompt must follow the separator, or load it with `--prompt-file`.
244: 
245: ---
246: 
247: ## 4. RULES
248: 
249: ### ✅ ALWAYS
250: 
251: 1. Verify Devin CLI is installed before first invocation (`command -v devin`).
252: 2. Delegate research and review lineages to `../../system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs` with executor kind `cli-devin`. It rejects every other loop type, so a single build or doc dispatch uses the child dispatch envelope in [providers-and-models.md](./references/providers-and-models.md) §5. Never build a second adapter in this packet.
253: 3. Use `--permission-mode auto` for review/analysis/research, and `--permission-mode dangerous` for code generation and file modification. `devin -p` itself defaults to `auto`, so omitting the flag causes a silent no-op on edit tasks.
254:     Prefer `dangerous` over `accept-edits` for any task that must read files or run its own verification; `accept-edits` refuses those calls and the dispatch fails silently.
255: 4. Validate Devin-generated code (XSS, injection, eval, syntax checks via `node --check`, `tsc --noEmit`, etc.) before applying.
256: 5. Capture stderr (`2>&1`) so rate-limit messages and errors surface.
257: 6. **Redirect devin stdin from `/dev/null` on EVERY non-interactive dispatch**, not only inside a `while read` loop, the condition this rule used to name and the reason it was skipped.
258:     Pattern: `devin -p -- "$PROMPT" > "$LOG" 2>&1 </dev/null &`. Without `</dev/null`, the backgrounded devin process inherits the loop's stdin and silently consumes the remaining lines.
259:     See `references/integration-patterns.md#background-execution` → "Silent Stdin Consumption".
260: 7. **Specify model + permission mode explicitly** — never rely on caller environment. Default: `--model swe --permission-mode dangerous`. Honor user overrides verbatim. Use `gpt-5-6-luna-max` for reasoning-heavy tasks (architecture, security, deep planning).
261: 8. Route to the appropriate subagent profile when the task matches a specialization (see Section 3 routing table); use `subagent_explore` for read-only research, `subagent_general` for code changes.
262: 9. **Pass the spec folder to the delegated agent** in the prompt: if the calling AI has an active Gate-3 spec folder, include `Spec folder: <path> (pre-approved, skip Gate 3)`. If none, ASK the user before delegating — the delegated agent cannot answer Gate 3 in non-interactive `-p` mode.
263: 10. **Prompt construction & model-craft (cli-* family precedence).** Compose every dispatch prompt via the 2-tier rule canonical in `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md`:
264:     1. **Fast path (default).** Build from the local `assets/prompt-quality-card.md`, which delegates the framework table + CLEAR check to the canonical card.
265:     2. **Deep path (escalation).** Dispatch `@prompt-improver` via the Task tool (never load full `sk-prompt` inline) when any canonical **Tier 2** trigger applies — the trigger list lives in `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md` under "Tier 2 — Deep path"; do not re-enumerate it here.
266: 11. **Never inject user-level voice/personalization content into AI-orchestrated Devin delegations.** Devin CLI reads user-level rules from `~/.config/devin/` and project `.devin/` config. When an AI delegates via `devin -p`, the calling AI's own voice rules govern the response. Do NOT read user config and paste into delegation prompts.
267:     Keep delegations focused on task/model/permission-mode/(spec-folder pre-approval). If the user asks how to make Devin sound more like another tool in *their own* sessions, point to `~/.config/devin/config.json`, not any repo asset.
268: 12. **Code Standards Loading (surface-aware contract)** — When dispatching for code review or code generation, instruct the dispatched session to:
269:     1. load `sk-code`;
270:     2. let `sk-code` emit a surface tag matching the detected stack from markers and target files;
271:     3. load the selected surface resources and run its verification commands;
272:     4. add `code-review` only for formal findings-first review output.
273:     Fallback: if the surface cannot be determined confidently, ask for the runtime surface and verification command set. NEVER hardcode obsolete sibling code skills in dispatch prompts.
274: 13. **Design Standards Loading (measured-reference contract)** — When dispatching for design or UI work, instruct the dispatched session to:
275:     1. load `sk-design-md-generator`;
276:     2. extract a measured Style Reference DESIGN.md from the live source before building UI, with named color tokens, type scale, components, Quick-Start CSS/Tailwind;
277:     3. build against those measured tokens and run the extraction's validate step to confirm hex/section fidelity.
278:     Fallback: if there is no live source to measure, ask for the reference URL or the exact tokens to build against. NEVER treat `mcp-figma` or `sk-design-md-generator` as a taste, visual-direction, or critique authority. The extraction measures real CSS, it does not judge design.
279: 14. **Pass the design reference manifest to the dispatched session.** When dispatching design or UI work, inline a `DESIGN_DISPATCH_MANIFEST v1` block in the prompt. The child cannot resolve skill paths, so the manifest travels in the payload, not by reference.
280:     It carries `styleReferenceExtracted` true, the live `source` that was measured, the measured design tokens / type scale / components the child must build against, `loadedFiles`, and `proofDemandBack`.
281:     If the manifest cannot be assembled, because no Style Reference was extracted or there is no live source to measure, ASK before launching the child rather than starting a silent design dispatch. The child returns the demanded proof; the parent reconciles it on the return path.
282: 15. **Single-dispatch discipline (operator-gated, session-scoped).** Default: launch ONE cli-* dispatch at a time across the cli-* family (cli-devin, cli-codex, cli-claude-code, cli-opencode, cli-cursor). Wait for the dispatched agent's work to return, verify outputs exist, then SIGKILL only the dispatch THIS skill started.
283:     - Capture the PID at launch (`devin -p -- ... & DEVIN_PID=$!`) and kill that captured PID directly plus its own orphan children (`kill -9 "$DEVIN_PID" 2>/dev/null; pkill -9 -P "$DEVIN_PID" 2>/dev/null`), then apply the same PID-scoped `gtimeout` cleanup.
284:     - **Never use a blanket `pkill -9 -f "devin -p"` pattern.** It kills EVERY running `devin` process on the machine, including the operator's unrelated devin sessions.
285:     - Only launch the next dispatch (this skill OR a sibling) after the prior one is dead and RSS has dropped.
286:     - **Within a deep-flow session** (deep-review / deep-research): the operator authorizes the whole multi-iteration session at start. Iterations chain back-to-back with kill-between as the safety mechanism, NOT a per-iteration confirmation prompt.
287:     - **Exception (cross-skill parallel)**: when the operator explicitly authorizes N parallel dispatches, run N concurrently, but still SIGKILL each by its own captured PID as its work returns.
288: 16. **Set `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1` in the dispatched child's env AND state the exemption in the prompt.** The variable makes the waiver true; it does not make it observable.
289:     The reader being waived is a model, and a model cannot see an environment variable, so a child given only the variable still stops to ask the documentation-scope question and writes nothing, at exit code zero.
290:     Copy the preamble from [`shared/references/child-dispatch-preamble.md`](../shared/references/child-dispatch-preamble.md) to the top of every non-interactive prompt.
291:     The variable also matters for the per-session worktree wrapper (`.skilled/bin/worktree-session.sh`). A dispatched `devin -p` is an orchestrated sub-session, not a new top-level session, so it must SHARE the parent's worktree, not allocate its own.
292:     The wrapper checks `AI_SESSION_CHILD` (plus a `git --git-common-dir` structural backstop) and exec's in place when set.
293:     Pattern: `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 devin -p -- ... </dev/null`. Harmless when the wrapper is not in use. See `.skilled/bin/README.md` → "Worktree session isolation".
294: 
295: 17. **Agent-persona injection (attach identity, not just the task).** Every dispatch composes `{resolved agent persona + task prompt}` — never a bare task.
296:     - Resolve the persona from the ACTIVE runtime's agent directory per AGENTS.md §9 (`.skilled/agents/<name>.md`, `.claude/agents/<name>.md`, etc. — never hardcode one runtime).
297:     - Map each subtask to the RIGHT agent (`code`→code, `review`→review, `design`→design, research→`deep-research`, docs→`markdown`), not one default.
298:     - **Devin has a native persona surface:** dispatch via `run_subagent` naming the resolved profile (`.devin/agents/<name>/AGENT.md` mirrors all 13 canonical agents; see "Agent Roster Parity"). Native resolution satisfies the rule.
299:     - On a bare top-level `devin -p` that names no subagent, **INLINE** the persona block into the payload using the same in-payload pattern as the `DESIGN_DISPATCH_MANIFEST` (Rule 14). The child cannot resolve agent paths by reference.
300:     - A persona-less dispatch runs the leaf as a generic assistant, silently dropping the agent's tool-scope, verification gates, and output contract.
301:     Canonical contract: `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md` "Persona Injection"; native precedent: `orchestrate.md` "Agent Loading Protocol". Rare exceptions (native surface used, focused summary for a small-context model, pure-mechanical command) are declared at the dispatch site.
302: 
303: ### ⛔ NEVER
304: 
305: 1. Use `--permission-mode dangerous` in a task the user has not approved it for (full shell beyond workspace = damage risk). One explicit approval covers every dispatch in that task, the default invocation included, and a new task needs a new approval. `accept-edits` (workspace edits auto-approve) does not require pre-approval.
306: 2. Trust Devin output blindly for security-sensitive code, send sensitive data (API keys, passwords, credentials) in prompts, or hammer the API with rapid sequential calls.
307: 3. Use Devin for tasks where context is already loaded — direct action by the calling AI is faster.
308: 4. Assume Devin output is correct without verification — cross-reference codebase and project standards.
309: 5. Build or maintain a packet-local Devin execution adapter; the deep-loop runtime is the execution authority.
310: 
311: ### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF
312: 
313: 1. Devin CLI is not installed and user has not acknowledged (provide `devin setup` or install URL).
314: 2. Rate limits are persistently exceeded (suggest checking the Devin account's plan and usage limits).
315: 3. Devin output conflicts with existing code patterns (present both perspectives; user decides).
316: 4. Task requires `--permission-mode dangerous` and the user has not approved it for this task (describe the risks and ask once for the whole task). `accept-edits` does not require escalation.
317: 5. Cloud handoff is requested for a task involving sensitive data or production systems (confirm the cloud session's isolation and data handling before handing off).

22: ## 1. WHEN TO USE

24: ### Activation Triggers

64:

71: ### Provider Auth Pre-Flight (Devin Account OAuth)
72: 
73: **MANDATORY before any first dispatch in a session.** cli-devin authenticates through Devin account OAuth only. If `devin auth login` has not been completed on this machine, a dispatch fails with an authentication error mid-round-trip. Run this check once per session, cache the result, and re-run it only if a dispatch fails with an auth error.

75: ```bash
76: # One-shot pre-flight: capture Devin auth status for routing
77: DEVIN_AUTH=$(devin auth status 2>&1)
78: echo "$DEVIN_AUTH" | grep -qi "logged in" && DEVIN_AUTH_OK=1 || DEVIN_AUTH_OK=0

81: **Decision tree** (apply in order — first match wins):

83: | State | DEVIN_AUTH_OK | Action |
84: |-------|---------------|--------|
85: | OAuth ready | 1 | Proceed with `devin -p --model <model> --permission-mode <mode> -- "<prompt>"` |
86: | Not logged in | 0 | **ASK user** to run `devin auth login` — surface the command, do NOT dispatch. Never substitute a different auth method or skip the check. |

94: ```

110: > **Why `dangerous` is the default for implementation work.** Under `accept-edits` Devin may
111: > edit files but every other tool call is refused with
112: > `warning: rejected a tool call that requires confirmation`. In a non-interactive `-p` session
113: > there is nobody to confirm, so the dispatch cannot read a module to check an export, cannot
114: > grep, and cannot run the tests it was asked to run. The observed failure is not an error —
115: > it is a dispatch that spends its whole budget exploring, writes nothing, and exits 0. A
116: > caller who does not diff the worktree afterwards will read that as success.
117: >
118: > The marginal risk is smaller than the name suggests: `accept-edits` already grants arbitrary
119: > file modification, which is the destructive capability. `dangerous` adds the ability to run
120: > commands, which is what lets the executor verify its own work instead of handing back
121: > unverified edits. Use `auto` for read-only review, analysis, and research, where no
122: > elevation is needed.
123: >
124: > **`auto` is read-only, not tool-free.** It refuses any tool call that wants confirmation,
125: > and a shell command counts even when the command only reads. Observed on 2026-09-15: a
126: > crawl dispatched under `auto` decided on its own to run a `git` command to check state,
127: > was refused with `warning: rejected a tool call that requires confirmation`, and exited 0
128: > having reported almost nothing. A research dispatch that might shell out therefore needs
129: > `dangerous` with a read-only instruction in the prompt, and the caller diffs the worktree
130: > afterwards to confirm it wrote nothing. Reserve `auto` for a dispatch whose whole job is
131: > reading files.

169: ### Devin Subagent Delegation
170: 
171: The calling AI is the conductor. Devin's `run_subagent` tool spawns independent workers that share tools and codebase context but operate in their own conversation chain.
172: 
173: Two built-in profiles (`subagent_explore` read-only, `subagent_general` full-access) plus custom `.devin/agents/[name]/AGENT.md` profiles shape HOW Devin processes the subtask.
174: 
175: Full roster and invocation patterns: [agent-delegation.md](./references/agent-delegation.md).
176: 
177: | Task Type | Profile | Model |
178: |-----------|---------|-------|
179: | Read-only codebase exploration | `subagent_explore` | Default subagent model (SWE-1.6) |
180: | General-purpose code changes | `subagent_general` | Same as parent agent |
181: | Custom specialized worker | `.devin/agents/[name]/AGENT.md` | Pinned in AGENT.md or default |
182: 
183: Subagents run foreground (parent pauses) or background (parallel, auto-deny unapproved tools). The `run_subagent` tool takes a profile, not a model — to pin a model on a write-capable subagent, use a custom AGENT.md with a `model:` field.

220: ### Dispatch-Critical Gotchas
221: 
222: The full flag glossary, permission modes, unique capabilities (`/handoff`, `run_subagent`, `devin mcp`, session resume/continue, `--sandbox`), essential command examples, and troubleshooting table are in the ALWAYS-loaded [cli-reference.md](./references/cli-reference.md). Four gotchas that silently break a dispatch and must be honored at routing time:
223: 
224: - **`devin -p` is non-interactive and exits after one turn** — it prints the response to stdout and exits. For multi-turn work, use `devin -c` (continue) or `devin -r <session-id>` (resume). Do not expect a REPL from `-p`.
225: - **`--permission-mode` defaults to `auto` (read-only auto-approve).** File-modification tasks silently prompt or no-op without elevated mode.
226:   - Pass `--permission-mode dangerous` whenever the task requires edits.
227:   - `accept-edits` is only half a grant. It permits writes but refuses the reads and commands an implementer needs, so a dispatch under it can burn its whole budget and exit 0 having written nothing.
228:   - The `--sandbox` flag selects `autonomous` mode, the only mode available in sandbox sessions.
229: - **`devin -p` rejects MCP tool calls under `auto`/`accept-edits`** (and `smart` may be unavailable). When a least-privilege MCP allowlist is preferable to blanket elevation, grant it in a machine-local config:
230: ```json
231: // .devin/config.local.json
232: { "permissions": { "allow": ["mcp__<server>__*"] } }
233: ```
234: Then `auto`/`accept-edits` auto-approve exactly those MCP tools; reserve `dangerous` for throwaway isolated runners.
235: - **Always pass `--model` explicitly in scripts** — omitting it relies on the caller's `~/.config/devin/config.json` default, which may be a different model. Explicit means reproducible regardless of who runs it.
236: - **Model ids carry no `-high` suffix, but the interactive picker shows one** — the TUI labels `glm-5-2` as "GLM-5.2 High", so an operator asking for "GLM 5.2 high" means the id `glm-5-2`. No `glm-5-2-high` exists. `devin models list` is the authority for every id and its display name; this document's roster is a convenience copy.
237: - **A free-tier model still dispatches when the Pro quota reads 0%** — `glm-5-2` is billed as Free, and a dispatch succeeded with `Pro · 0% remaining` showing in the TUI. Quota exhaustion gates the paid families, so do not abandon a dispatch on the quota banner alone; probe with a trivial read-only call first.
238: - **`devin --help` is NOT the authoritative `--permission-mode` enum.** It prints 4 values; the binary accepts 8.
239:   - Canonical set with aliases: `normal` (`auto`), `accept-edits`, `smart`, `dangerous` (`yolo`, `bypass`), `autonomous` (requires `--sandbox`).
240:   - Do not "correct" a mode value in this skill because help omits it. That conclusion is wrong and has been reached before.
241:   - Probe instead: `devin --permission-mode <value> --prompt-file /nonexistent` (exit 2 = rejected, exit 1 = accepted).
242:   - The enum also moves between releases, so re-probe after an upgrade rather than trusting either help or this line.
243: - **Use `--` before every print-mode prompt** — `devin -p -- "list all TODO comments"` prevents the prompt from being parsed as CLI flags. The prompt must follow the separator, or load it with `--prompt-file`.

247: ## 4. RULES
248: 
249: ### ✅ ALWAYS
250: 
251: 1. Verify Devin CLI is installed before first invocation (`command -v devin`).
252: 2. Delegate research and review lineages to `../../system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs` with executor kind `cli-devin`. It rejects every other loop type, so a single build or doc dispatch uses the child dispatch envelope in [providers-and-models.md](./references/providers-and-models.md) §5. Never build a second adapter in this packet.
253: 3. Use `--permission-mode auto` for review/analysis/research, and `--permission-mode dangerous` for code generation and file modification. `devin -p` itself defaults to `auto`, so omitting the flag causes a silent no-op on edit tasks.
254:     Prefer `dangerous` over `accept-edits` for any task that must read files or run its own verification; `accept-edits` refuses those calls and the dispatch fails silently.
255: 4. Validate Devin-generated code (XSS, injection, eval, syntax checks via `node --check`, `tsc --noEmit`, etc.) before applying.
256: 5. Capture stderr (`2>&1`) so rate-limit messages and errors surface.
257: 6. **Redirect devin stdin from `/dev/null` on EVERY non-interactive dispatch**, not only inside a `while read` loop, the condition this rule used to name and the reason it was skipped.
258:     Pattern: `devin -p -- "$PROMPT" > "$LOG" 2>&1 </dev/null &`. Without `</dev/null`, the backgrounded devin process inherits the loop's stdin and silently consumes the remaining lines.
259:     See `references/integration-patterns.md#background-execution` → "Silent Stdin Consumption".
260: 7. **Specify model + permission mode explicitly** — never rely on caller environment. Default: `--model swe --permission-mode dangerous`. Honor user overrides verbatim. Use `gpt-5-6-luna-max` for reasoning-heavy tasks (architecture, security, deep planning).
261: 8. Route to the appropriate subagent profile when the task matches a specialization (see Section 3 routing table); use `subagent_explore` for read-only research, `subagent_general` for code changes.
262: 9. **Pass the spec folder to the delegated agent** in the prompt: if the calling AI has an active Gate-3 spec folder, include `Spec folder: <path> (pre-approved, skip Gate 3)`. If none, ASK the user before delegating — the delegated agent cannot answer Gate 3 in non-interactive `-p` mode.
263: 10. **Prompt construction & model-craft (cli-* family precedence).** Compose every dispatch prompt via the 2-tier rule canonical in `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md`:
264:     1. **Fast path (default).** Build from the local `assets/prompt-quality-card.md`, which delegates the framework table + CLEAR check to the canonical card.
265:     2. **Deep path (escalation).** Dispatch `@prompt-improver` via the Task tool (never load full `sk-prompt` inline) when any canonical **Tier 2** trigger applies — the trigger list lives in `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md` under "Tier 2 — Deep path"; do not re-enumerate it here.
266: 11. **Never inject user-level voice/personalization content into AI-orchestrated Devin delegations.** Devin CLI reads user-level rules from `~/.config/devin/` and project `.devin/` config. When an AI delegates via `devin -p`, the calling AI's own voice rules govern the response. Do NOT read user config and paste into delegation prompts.
267:     Keep delegations focused on task/model/permission-mode/(spec-folder pre-approval). If the user asks how to make Devin sound more like another tool in *their own* sessions, point to `~/.config/devin/config.json`, not any repo asset.
268: 12. **Code Standards Loading (surface-aware contract)** — When dispatching for code review or code generation, instruct the dispatched session to:
269:     1. load `sk-code`;
270:     2. let `sk-code` emit a surface tag matching the detected stack from markers and target files;
271:     3. load the selected surface resources and run its verification commands;
272:     4. add `code-review` only for formal findings-first review output.
273:     Fallback: if the surface cannot be determined confidently, ask for the runtime surface and verification command set. NEVER hardcode obsolete sibling code skills in dispatch prompts.
274: 13. **Design Standards Loading (measured-reference contract)** — When dispatching for design or UI work, instruct the dispatched session to:
275:     1. load `sk-design-md-generator`;
276:     2. extract a measured Style Reference DESIGN.md from the live source before building UI, with named color tokens, type scale, components, Quick-Start CSS/Tailwind;
277:     3. build against those measured tokens and run the extraction's validate step to confirm hex/section fidelity.
278:     Fallback: if there is no live source to measure, ask for the reference URL or the exact tokens to build against. NEVER treat `mcp-figma` or `sk-design-md-generator` as a taste, visual-direction, or critique authority. The extraction measures real CSS, it does not judge design.
279: 14. **Pass the design reference manifest to the dispatched session.** When dispatching design or UI work, inline a `DESIGN_DISPATCH_MANIFEST v1` block in the prompt. The child cannot resolve skill paths, so the manifest travels in the payload, not by reference.
280:     It carries `styleReferenceExtracted` true, the live `source` that was measured, the measured design tokens / type scale / components the child must build against, `loadedFiles`, and `proofDemandBack`.
281:     If the manifest cannot be assembled, because no Style Reference was extracted or there is no live source to measure, ASK before launching the child rather than starting a silent design dispatch. The child returns the demanded proof; the parent reconciles it on the return path.
282: 15. **Single-dispatch discipline (operator-gated, session-scoped).** Default: launch ONE cli-* dispatch at a time across the cli-* family (cli-devin, cli-codex, cli-claude-code, cli-opencode, cli-cursor). Wait for the dispatched agent's work to return, verify outputs exist, then SIGKILL only the dispatch THIS skill started.
283:     - Capture the PID at launch (`devin -p -- ... & DEVIN_PID=$!`) and kill that captured PID directly plus its own orphan children (`kill -9 "$DEVIN_PID" 2>/dev/null; pkill -9 -P "$DEVIN_PID" 2>/dev/null`), then apply the same PID-scoped `gtimeout` cleanup.
284:     - **Never use a blanket `pkill -9 -f "devin -p"` pattern.** It kills EVERY running `devin` process on the machine, including the operator's unrelated devin sessions.
285:     - Only launch the next dispatch (this skill OR a sibling) after the prior one is dead and RSS has dropped.
286:     - **Within a deep-flow session** (deep-review / deep-research): the operator authorizes the whole multi-iteration session at start. Iterations chain back-to-back with kill-between as the safety mechanism, NOT a per-iteration confirmation prompt.
287:     - **Exception (cross-skill parallel)**: when the operator explicitly authorizes N parallel dispatches, run N concurrently, but still SIGKILL each by its own captured PID as its work returns.
288: 16. **Set `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1` in the dispatched child's env AND state the exemption in the prompt.** The variable makes the waiver true; it does not make it observable.
289:     The reader being waived is a model, and a model cannot see an environment variable, so a child given only the variable still stops to ask the documentation-scope question and writes nothing, at exit code zero.
290:     Copy the preamble from [`shared/references/child-dispatch-preamble.md`](../shared/references/child-dispatch-preamble.md) to the top of every non-interactive prompt.
291:     The variable also matters for the per-session worktree wrapper (`.skilled/bin/worktree-session.sh`). A dispatched `devin -p` is an orchestrated sub-session, not a new top-level session, so it must SHARE the parent's worktree, not allocate its own.
292:     The wrapper checks `AI_SESSION_CHILD` (plus a `git --git-common-dir` structural backstop) and exec's in place when set.
293:     Pattern: `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 devin -p -- ... </dev/null`. Harmless when the wrapper is not in use. See `.skilled/bin/README.md` → "Worktree session isolation".
294: 
295: 17. **Agent-persona injection (attach identity, not just the task).** Every dispatch composes `{resolved agent persona + task prompt}` — never a bare task.
296:     - Resolve the persona from the ACTIVE runtime's agent directory per AGENTS.md §9 (`.skilled/agents/<name>.md`, `.claude/agents/<name>.md`, etc. — never hardcode one runtime).
297:     - Map each subtask to the RIGHT agent (`code`→code, `review`→review, `design`→design, research→`deep-research`, docs→`markdown`), not one default.
298:     - **Devin has a native persona surface:** dispatch via `run_subagent` naming the resolved profile (`.devin/agents/<name>/AGENT.md` mirrors all 13 canonical agents; see "Agent Roster Parity"). Native resolution satisfies the rule.
299:     - On a bare top-level `devin -p` that names no subagent, **INLINE** the persona block into the payload using the same in-payload pattern as the `DESIGN_DISPATCH_MANIFEST` (Rule 14). The child cannot resolve agent paths by reference.
300:     - A persona-less dispatch runs the leaf as a generic assistant, silently dropping the agent's tool-scope, verification gates, and output contract.
301:     Canonical contract: `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md` "Persona Injection"; native precedent: `orchestrate.md` "Agent Loading Protocol". Rare exceptions (native surface used, focused summary for a small-context model, pure-mechanical command) are declared at the dispatch site.

303: ### ⛔ NEVER
304: 
305: 1. Use `--permission-mode dangerous` in a task the user has not approved it for (full shell beyond workspace = damage risk). One explicit approval covers every dispatch in that task, the default invocation included, and a new task needs a new approval. `accept-edits` (workspace edits auto-approve) does not require pre-approval.
306: 2. Trust Devin output blindly for security-sensitive code, send sensitive data (API keys, passwords, credentials) in prompts, or hammer the API with rapid sequential calls.
307: 3. Use Devin for tasks where context is already loaded — direct action by the calling AI is faster.
308: 4. Assume Devin output is correct without verification — cross-reference codebase and project standards.
309: 5. Build or maintain a packet-local Devin execution adapter; the deep-loop runtime is the execution authority.

312: 
313: 1. Devin CLI is not installed and user has not acknowledged (provide `devin setup` or install URL).
314: 2. Rate limits are persistently exceeded (suggest checking the Devin account's plan and usage limits).
315: 3. Devin output conflicts with existing code patterns (present both perspectives; user decides).
316: 4. Task requires `--permission-mode dangerous` and the user has not approved it for this task (describe the risks and ask once for the whole task). `accept-edits` does not require escalation.
317: 5. Cloud handoff is requested for a task involving sensitive data or production systems (confirm the cloud session's isolation and data handling before handing off).

16: # Devin CLI - Complete Command Reference
17: 
18: Comprehensive reference for all Devin CLI commands, flags, models, configuration, and troubleshooting.
19: 
20: ---
21: 
22: ## 1. OVERVIEW
23: 
24: ### Purpose
25: 
26: Be the single source a dispatcher checks before running Devin, so every option a run depends on, permission modes included, is looked up rather than remembered.
27: 
28: ### When to Use
29: 
30: - Setting up or configuring Devin CLI
31: - Looking up command-line flags, subcommands, or permission modes
32: - Troubleshooting authentication, sandbox, or session issues
33: - Configuring subagents via `.devin/agents/[name]/AGENT.md`
34: - Selecting the right permission mode for a task
35: 
36: ### Core Principle
37: 
38: Devin CLI is Cognition's terminal-based AI coding agent — a fast, minimal agent that lives both in the terminal and in the cloud. It fronts a broad multi-model surface; this skill curates seven families in scope — DeepSeek, Gemini, GLM-5.2, GPT-5.6 (Luna Max), GPT-6 (Luna Max), Grok (4.5 and 4.6), and SWE-2 (full catalog: [providers-and-models.md](./providers-and-models.md)). Devin's native Adaptive model router and its full 48-family roster remain available via `devin models list` but are out of this skill's curated scope. The skill dispatches `swe` (alias → `swe-2`) at `accept-edits` permission mode by default; users can override the model and mode. It provides direct access to multi-model coding, subagent delegation, cloud handoff, MCP integration, and session management — all governed by configurable permission modes.
39: 
40: ### Key Sources
41: 
42: | Source | URL |
43: |--------|-----|
44: | **Documentation** | [docs.devin.ai/cli](https://docs.devin.ai/cli) |
45: | **Web App** | [app.devin.ai](https://app.devin.ai) |
46: | **Runtime** | Node.js / native binary |
47: | **Version** | 3000.2.17 |
48:

50: 
51: ## 2. INSTALLATION
52: 
53: | Method | Command | Notes |
54: |--------|---------|-------|
55: | **Interactive setup** | `devin setup` | Wizard for auth + MCP configuration |
56: | **Direct install** | `curl -fsSL https://devin.ai/install \| bash` | Persistent install |
57: | **Update** | `devin update` | Check for and install updates |
58: | **Force update** | `devin update --force` | Re-install even if on latest version |
59: 
60: **Platform support:**
61: 
62: | Platform | Status |
63: |----------|--------|
64: | macOS | Full support (sandbox via Seatbelt, works out of the box) |
65: | Linux | Full support (sandbox requires `bwrap` + `socat`) |
66: | Windows (WSL) | Use WSL 2; native Windows cannot run the sandbox |
67: 
68: After installation, run `devin` for the interactive REPL or `devin -p -- "prompt"` for non-interactive use.

72: ## 3. AUTHENTICATION
73: 
74: cli-devin authenticates through **Devin account OAuth only** — `devin auth login` (browser flow). It does not use an API key.
75: 
76: **OAuth login/logout:**
77: 
78: ```bash
79: # Authenticate via Devin account (opens browser)
80: devin auth login
81: 
82: # For SSH/remote sessions (skip browser, manually paste token)
83: devin auth login --force-manual-token-flow
84: 
85: # View authentication status
86: devin auth status
87: 
88: # Log out and clear stored credentials
89: devin auth logout
90: ```
91: 
92: **Auth status output:**
93: 
94: ```
95: Logged in (via Devin).
96: 
97: Credentials:
98:   File:              ~/.local/share/devin/credentials.toml

105: 
106: ## 4. COMMAND-LINE FLAGS
107: 
108: ### Essential Flags
109: 
110: | Flag | Short | Values | Description |
111: |------|-------|--------|-------------|
112: | `--model` | | `<model-name>` | Model to use — `swe` (default alias → `swe-2`), plus the curated DeepSeek / GLM-5.2 / GPT-5.6 Luna Max / GPT-6 Luna Max / Grok (4.5 and 4.6) / SWE-2 families (see §5) |
113: | `--permission-mode` | | canonical: `normal`, `accept-edits`, `smart`, `dangerous`, `autonomous` — aliases: `auto`→`normal`, `yolo`/`bypass`→`dangerous` | Permission mode controlling tool auto-approval. **`devin --help` prints only 4 of these 8 accepted values** — it is not the authoritative enum. See the probe below. |
114: | `--print` | `-p` | `[<prompt>]` | Non-interactive mode: print response and exit |
115: | `--continue` | `-c` | (none) | Continue the most recent session in the current directory |
116: | `--resume` | `-r` | `[<session-id>]` | Resume a specific session by ID, or select interactively |
117: | `--sandbox` | | (none) | Enable OS-level process sandboxing (selects `autonomous` permission mode) |
118: | `--prompt-file` | | `<file>` | Load the initial prompt from a file |
119: | `--config` | | `<path>` | Configuration file path (override default `~/.config/devin/config.json`) |
120: | `--export` | | `[<path>]` | Export conversation to a file after each turn (ATIF format) |
121: | `--agent-config` | | `<file>` | Declarative agent configuration file (JSON or YAML) |
122: | `--respect-workspace-trust` | | `true`, `false` | Respect workspace trust settings |
123: 
124: > **Verifying a flag value without spending a session.** `--help` under-reports the
125: > `--permission-mode` enum, so never conclude a value is invalid because help omits it.
126: > Force parse-time validation instead: an invalid value fails at exit 2 before the file
127: > is read, a valid one reaches the file error at exit 1.
128: >
129: > ```bash
130: > devin --permission-mode <value> --prompt-file /nonexistent
131: > #   exit 2 + "invalid value ..."        -> rejected by the binary
132: > #   exit 1 + "Failed to read prompt file" -> accepted
133: > ```
134: >
135: > Verified against `devin 3000.6.7`: `auto`, `normal`, `accept-edits`, `smart`,
136: > `dangerous`, `yolo`, `bypass`, `autonomous` all accepted; `plan` and `manual`
137: > (Claude's modes, not Devin's) rejected. Re-run the probe after a CLI upgrade —
138: > `smart` was rejected at 3000.2.17 and is accepted at 3000.6.7.
139: 
140: ### Prompt Syntax
141: 
142: ```bash
143: # Interactive REPL (no prompt)
144: devin
145: 
146: # Start REPL with initial prompt (use -- before the prompt)
147: devin -- your prompt here
148: 
149: # Non-interactive: print mode
150: devin -p -- "prompt"
151: devin -p -- "prompt words here"    # Same, using -- separator
152: ```
153: 
154: ### Permission Mode Values
155: 
156: | Value | Behavior | Best For |
157: |-------|----------|----------|
158: | `auto` | Auto-approves read-only tools; prompts for writes and shell | Review, analysis, research |
159: | `accept-edits` | Auto-approves workspace edits + read-only; prompts for shell | Code generation, bug fixing, documentation |
160: | `smart` | Auto-runs actions a fast model judges safe | Trusted workflows with judgment calls |
161: | `dangerous` | Auto-approves all tools without prompting | Full trust — **requires explicit user approval** |
162: | `autonomous` | Sandbox-enforced; only available with `--sandbox` | Unattended execution with OS-level limits |
163: 
164: ### Usage Examples
165: 
166: ```bash
167: # Interactive REPL
168: devin
169: 
170: # Non-interactive with model selection
171: devin -p --model gpt-5-6-luna-max -- "Refactor utils.ts to use async/await"
172: 
173: # With permission mode for file edits
174: devin -p --permission-mode accept-edits -- "Add error handling to auth.ts"
175: 
176: # Continue the most recent session
177: devin -c
178: 
179: # Resume a specific session
180: devin -r brisk-otter
181: 
182: # With OS-level sandbox
183: devin --sandbox -p -- "Run the test suite and fix failures"
184: 
185: # Load prompt from file
186: devin -p --prompt-file ./prompt.txt
187: 
188: # Export conversation
189: devin --export out.json -- fix the tests
190: 
191: # Start REPL with initial prompt
192: devin -- add a login page
193: ```

195: ---
196: 
197: ## 5. MODEL SELECTION
198: 
199: ### Supported Models
200: 
201: Devin dispatches **`swe`** (alias → `swe-2`) at the **`accept-edits`** permission mode by default. The model is switched per-dispatch with `--model <alias>` (short names resolve to the latest version in that family). There is no headless reasoning-effort flag — depth is expressed through the permission mode (autonomy) and the chosen model, not a reasoning flag; interactive REPL sessions cycle thinking depth with `Alt+T` (macOS: `Opt+T`).
202: 
203: **Full curated roster (DeepSeek / Gemini / GLM-5.2 / GPT-5.6 Luna Max / SWE-2 families) → [providers-and-models.md](./providers-and-models.md).** Devin's native Adaptive router and full 48-family roster are out of this skill's curated scope.
204: 
205: ### Setting the Model
206: 
207: ```bash
208: # Command flag
209: devin --model gpt-5-6-luna-max -- refactor this module
210: devin --model glm-5-2 -- explain this code
211: devin -p --model swe -- "list all TODO comments"
212: 
213: # Slash command (inside REPL)
214: /model gpt-5-6-luna-max
215: /model glm-5-2
216: /model deepseek-v4-flash-max
217: 
218: # Config file (~/.config/devin/config.json)
219: {
220:   "agent": {
221:     "model": "swe"
222:   }
223: }
224: ```
225: 
226: ### Selection Strategy
227: 
228: | Task Type | Model | Rationale |
229: |-----------|-------|-----------|
230: | Architecture decisions | `gpt-5-6-luna-max` | Multi-faceted analysis benefits from deep reasoning |
231: | Security audits | `gpt-5-6-luna-max` | Catches subtle vulnerability patterns |
232: | Complex planning | `gpt-5-6-luna-max` / `glm-5-2-max` | Multi-strategy evaluation benefits from depth |
233: | Code generation | `glm-5-2` / `glm-5-2-max` | Balanced for most generation tasks |
234: | Standard code review | `glm-5-2` / `swe-2-high` | Efficient for pattern-based review |
235: | Implementation | `glm-5-2` / `swe-2-high` | Balanced for translating specs to code |
236: | Test generation | `swe-2-high` / `glm-5-2` | Solid test structure output |
237: | Documentation | `glm-5-2` / `swe` | Efficient for structured doc generation |
238: | Quick edits / lookups | `swe-2-medium` | Lowest-effort SWE-2 tier, free |
239: | Lowest latency, cost accepted | `swe-1-7-lightning` | The only lightning tier; metered, not free |
240: | Cost-sensitive work | `swe` / `swe-2-medium` | SWE-2 is free across all three effort tiers |
241: 
242: Always specify `--model` explicitly in scripts for predictability; omitting it relies on the CLI default from `~/.config/devin/config.json`, which may differ across machines.
243: 
244: ---

246: ## 6. OUTPUT HANDLING
247: 
248: ### Print Mode Output
249: 
250: `devin -p` writes its output to stdout. Use shell redirection or command substitution to capture it.
251: 
252: ```bash
253: # Capture to file
254: devin -p \
255:   --model swe \
256:   -- \
257:   "Generate a TypeScript interface for the User model" > /tmp/user-interface.ts
258: 
259: # Capture to variable
260: RESULT=$(devin -p --model swe -- "List all exported functions in src/")
261: echo "$RESULT"
262: 
263: # Pipe to another command
264: devin -p --model swe -- "Generate SQL schema for users table" | psql -d mydb -f -
265: 
266: # Redirect stderr separately
267: devin -p --model swe -- "Analyze auth flow" > /tmp/analysis.txt 2>/tmp/errors.txt
268: ```
269: 
270: ### Export Format
271: 
272: Use `--export` to save the full conversation in ATIF format:
273: 
274: ```bash
275: # Export to default path
276: devin --export -- fix the tests
277: 
278: # Export to specific file
279: devin --export out.json -- fix tests
280: ```

283: 
284: | Code | Meaning |
285: |------|---------|
286: | `0` | Success |

400: ## 9. CONFIGURATION FILES
401: 
402: ### Directory Structure
403: 
404: ```
405: .devin/
406: ├── config.json          # Project-level CLI configuration
407: ├── config.local.json    # Local override (not shared with team)
408: ├── hooks/               # Lifecycle hooks
409: └── agents/
410:     └── [name]/
411:         └── AGENT.md     # Custom subagent profile
412: ```
413: 
414: ### config.json Format
415: 
416: ```json
417: // .devin/config.json or ~/.config/devin/config.json
418: {
419:   "agent": {
420:     "model": "swe"
421:   },
422:   "permissions": {
423:     "allow": [
424:       "Read(src/**)",
425:       "Write(src/**)",
426:       "Exec(git)",
427:       "Exec(npm run)"
428:     ],
429:     "deny": [
430:       "Exec(rm -rf)",
431:       "Exec(sudo)"
432:     ]
433:   },
434:   "mcpServers": {
435:     "my-server": {
436:       "command": "npx",
437:       "args": ["@company/mcp-server"],
438:       "transport": "stdio"
439:     }
440:   }
441: }
442: ```
443: 
444: ### Permission Syntax
445: 
446: **Scope-based:**
447: 
448: | Matcher | Controls | Example |
449: |---------|----------|---------|
450: | `Read(glob)` | File read access | `Read(src/**)` |
451: | `Write(glob)` | File write access | `Write(src/**)` |
452: | `Exec(prefix)` | Shell command execution | `Exec(git)`, `Exec(npm run)` |
453: | `Fetch(pattern)` | HTTP fetch access | `Fetch(https://api.github.com/*)` |
454: 
455: **Tool-based:** `read`, `edit`, `grep`, `glob`, `exec`
456: 
457: **MCP tool-based:** `mcp__server__tool`, `mcp__server__*`, `mcp__*`
458: 
459: ### Permission Precedence
460: 
461: 1. Organization/team settings (if enterprise) — highest
462: 2. Session-level grants (interactive approvals)
463: 3. Project local config (`.devin/config.local.json`)
464: 4. Project config (`.devin/config.json`)
465: 5. User config (`~/.config/devin/config.json`) — lowest
466: 
467: Deny is checked before ask, and ask is checked before allow. A deny rule always wins.
468: 
469: ---
470: 
471: ## 10. PERMISSION MODES
472: 
473: Permission modes control what the agent can do without asking for approval. Always choose the least-permissive mode that allows the task to complete.
474: 
475: ### Mode Reference
476: 
477: | Mode | Flag | Read-only | Fetch | Bash | File edits | Use Case |
478: |------|------|-----------|-------|------|------------|----------|
479: | **Auto** | `auto` | Auto | Prompt | Prompt | Prompt | Analysis, review, exploration |
480: | **Accept Edits** | `accept-edits` | Auto | Prompt | Prompt | Auto (workspace) | Code generation, refactoring |
481: | **Smart** | `smart` | Auto | Safe actions | Safe actions | Auto (workspace) | Trusted workflows with judgment |
482: | **Dangerous** | `dangerous` | Auto | Auto | Auto | Auto | Full trust — **requires explicit approval** |
483: | **Autonomous** | `autonomous` (+ `--sandbox`) | Auto | Auto (sandbox) | Auto (sandbox) | Prompt (edit/write tools bypass sandbox) | Unattended execution with OS limits |
484: 
485: ### Safety Guidance
486: 
487: ```bash
488: # SAFE: Auto mode for analysis
489: devin -p --permission-mode auto --model swe -- "Map the authentication flow"
490: 
491: # STANDARD: Accept Edits for code changes
492: devin -p --permission-mode accept-edits --model swe -- "Add error handling to all API routes"
493: 
494: # ELEVATED RISK: Dangerous mode — use only with explicit approval
495: devin -p --permission-mode dangerous --model gpt-5-6-luna-max -- "Migrate database schema"
496: 
497: # AUTONOMOUS: OS-enforced sandbox
498: devin --sandbox -p --model swe -- "Run the test suite and fix failures"
499: ```
500: 
501: ### Bypass vs Autonomous
502: 
503: | | Bypass (`dangerous`) | Autonomous (`--sandbox`) |
504: |---|---|---|
505: | Requires `--sandbox` | No | Yes (only available in sandbox sessions) |
506: | Shell commands | Auto-approved, unrestricted | Auto-approved, contained by sandbox |
507: | File writes via edit/write tools | Auto-approved anywhere | Still prompt (granting a scope expands the sandbox) |
508: | Network access | Unrestricted | Filtered by sandbox domain allow/deny lists |
509: | Respects admin Team Settings | Yes | Yes |
510: 
511: Pick `dangerous` when you trust the agent with your whole machine. Pick `--sandbox` (autonomous) when you want unattended execution with OS-enforced limits.
512: 
513: ---
514: 
515: ## 11. SESSION MANAGEMENT
516: 
517: ### Session Subcommands
518: 
519: | Subcommand | Description |
520: |------------|-------------|
521: | `devin` | Launch REPL; session picker available |
522: | `devin -c` | Continue the most recent session in the current directory |
523: | `devin -r` | Resume — pick from recent sessions interactively |
524: | `devin -r <session-id>` | Resume a specific session by ID |
525: | `devin list` | List sessions in the current directory (alias: `devin ls`) |
526: | `devin list --format json` | Output sessions as JSON |
527: | `devin list --format csv` | Output sessions as CSV |
528: 
529: ### Session Picker
530: 
531: Running `devin` without arguments opens the REPL. Use `/resume` inside the REPL to open the interactive session picker, or `/continue` to resume the most recent session.
532: 
533: ### Scripted Session Resume
534: 
535: ```bash
536: # Continue the most recent session non-interactively
537: devin -c -p "Continue implementing the rate limiter" --model swe
538: 
539: # Resume a specific session
540: devin -r brisk-otter -p "Continue from where we left off" --model swe
541: 
542: # List sessions as JSON for scripting
543: devin list --format json
544: ```
545: 
546: ### When to Use Each Operation
547: 
548: | Operation | When to Use |
549: |-----------|-------------|
550: | `-c` / `--continue` | Continue the most recent session with existing context |
551: | `-r` / `--resume` | Resume a specific session by ID |
552: | `/fork` | Fork the current session to try a different approach |
553: | `/revert` | Revert file changes from a specific step and rewind conversation |
554: | New session | Fresh context; previous session is not relevant |
555: | `-p` (stateless) | One-shot tasks; simpler to re-provide context than manage sessions |
556: 
557: ---
558: 
559: ## 12. SUBCOMMANDS
560: 
561: | Subcommand | Description |
562: |------------|-------------|
563: | `devin auth` | Authentication (login, logout, status) |
564: | `devin mcp` | MCP server management (add, list, get, remove, login, logout, enable, disable) |
565: | `devin models` | List available models organized by family |
566: | `devin rules` | Manage agent rules (always-on context blobs) |
567: | `devin skills` | Manage agent skills (slash commands and context blobs) |
568: | `devin plugins` | Manage plugins (install, list, info, update, remove) |
569: | `devin cloud` | Manage Devin Cloud resources (DRS: environment blueprints, sandbox sessions, builds) |
570: | `devin list` | List sessions in the current directory (alias: `ls`) |
571: | `devin update` | Check for and optionally install updates |
572: | `devin version` | Print the current version |
573: | `devin migrate` | Migrate configuration from other tools |
574: | `devin sandbox` | Process sandboxing for the exec tool (research preview) |
575: | `devin setup` | Interactive setup wizard |
576: | `devin uninstall` | Uninstall and remove data |
577: | `devin acp` | Run as an ACP (Agent Client Protocol) server over stdio |
578: | `devin shell` | Shell integration (init, run, setup) |
579: 
580: ---
581: 
582: ## 13. TROUBLESHOOTING
583: 
584: | Problem | Cause | Solution |
585: |---------|-------|----------|
586: | `not authenticated` / auth error | Devin account OAuth not configured | Run `devin auth login` (browser flow) |
587: | `Authentication failed` | OAuth session expired or invalid | Re-run `devin auth login` to re-authenticate |
588: | `Command not found: devin` | Not installed or not in PATH | Run `devin setup` or `curl -fsSL https://devin.ai/install \| bash`; verify with `which devin` |
589: | Task ran but no files changed | `devin -p` defaulted to `auto` (read-only) | Add `--permission-mode accept-edits` or `dangerous` |
590: | Session resume fails | Session ID invalid or expired | List sessions via `devin list`; start a new session |
591: | Slow response | Large context or complex task | Break task into smaller steps; use `auto` for analysis; use `swe-2-medium` for quick lookups, or `swe-1-7-lightning` when latency matters more than cost |
592: | `--sandbox` fails to start | Platform prerequisites missing | Run `devin sandbox setup` (Linux needs `bwrap` + `socat`; macOS works out of the box) |
593: | Cloud handoff fails | Network issue or uncommitted changes blocking | Commit or stash unwanted changes; verify connectivity to `app.devin.ai` |
594: | Subagent denied tools | Background subagent cannot prompt for permissions | Resume the subagent in the foreground to approve tools |
595: | MCP server not responding | Server not running or misconfigured | Check `devin mcp list`; verify server config in `.devin/config.json` |
596: | Windows compatibility | WSL not configured | Use WSL 2; native Windows cannot run the sandbox |
597: 
598: ---
599: 
600: ## 14. ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES
601: 
602: | Variable | Purpose | Example |
603: |----------|---------|---------|
604: | `DEVIN_MODEL` | Default model override | `swe`, `glm-5-2`, `gpt-5-6-luna-max` |
605: | `DEVIN_PERMISSION_MODE` | Default permission mode | `auto`, `accept-edits`, `smart`, `dangerous` |
606: | `DEVIN_SANDBOX` | Enable sandbox | `1` |
607: | `DEVIN_PROJECT_DIR` | Project root directory (set automatically by Devin on session start) | `/path/to/project` |
608: | `WINDSURF_API_KEY` | ACP server credentials (alternative to stored auth) | API key string |
